outcome: On 6 October 2026 OpenAI released, in its openai/math repository, a manuscript 'The Falconer distance conjecture in all dimensions' claiming a full proof for every d >= 2 and compact E in R^d with dim_H E > d/2, with a Lean 4 formalisation that a third-party Comparator run reports as accepted; no specialist in the area has publicly checked the argument, it is unrefereed, and the rest of the literature since January 2024 consists of partial results (planar pinned and regular-case results, pinned thresholds above d/2 for d >= 3, restricted classes, dimension-only bounds) plus discounted analogues.
problem_asks: Read from the frozen Wikipedia statement alone: (a) for every integer dimension d >= 2 (the bullet does not fix d, so this includes the planar case d = 2 and every d >= 3); (b) for every set E in R^d with Hausdorff dimension strictly greater than d/2 (the bullet says 'sets' and does not say compact or Borel; the literature states the conjecture for compact or Borel sets, and the OpenAI manuscript and Lean statement restrict to compact sets); (c) the conclusion that the distance set {|x - y| : x, y in E} has nonzero (positive) Lebesgue measure in R. Taken together this is one universal claim: the full conjecture, with the strict inequality (the endpoint dim_H E = d/2 is not asked). The bullet does not list separate sub-questions; the planar case, each d >= 3, and the compact-versus-general-set reduction are instances of the one claim.

events.what_happened: Falconer proved that compact or Borel sets in R^d with Hausdorff dimension above (d+1)/2 have distance sets of positive Lebesgue measure, and gave lattice-based examples with distance sets of measure zero in dimension s = d/2 and below, which is why d/2 is the conjectured threshold. Published in Mathematika (32(2), 1986 per the Wikipedia citation). Not opened directly; taken from the Wikipedia article and the OpenAI manuscript's introduction (which cites it as Falconer1985).
events.delivers: Positive Lebesgue measure of the distance set for Borel sets with dim_H E > (d+1)/2 in every d >= 2. Lattice example shows the exponent d/2 cannot be lowered.
events.remains: Everything between (d+1)/2 and d/2; the conjecture itself.

checked_by.who: Mathematika (journal of record, per the Wikipedia citation)
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the result (Mathematika 32(2), 1986 per Wikipedia citation); not independently re-checked here

events.direction: Partial result toward the conjecture; the threshold d/2 is the claimed sharp value, and this result is above it.
events.object: Lattice-based example of a set of dimension d/2 (and below) whose distance set has measure zero. Explicit construction, cited in the literature; not reviewed here.

events.what_happened: Bourgain improved the planar Falconer threshold from 3/2 to 13/9 (distance-set positive measure for planar sets above 13/9). Cited in the OpenAI manuscript's introduction as Bourgain1994 (planar and three-dimensional improvements via sphere restriction) and in search summaries. Not opened directly.
events.delivers: Planar sets with dim_H E > 13/9 have distance sets of positive Lebesgue measure (per secondary summaries). Planar case only.
events.remains: Planar sets with dimension in (13/9, 2] are covered by later work; d >= 3 and the planar conjecture at 1 remain open.
events.direction: Partial result toward the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Wolff proved that compact planar sets of Hausdorff dimension above 4/3 have distance sets of positive Lebesgue measure. Cited as Wolff1999 in the OpenAI manuscript's introduction and in the Wikipedia article's table. Not opened directly.
events.delivers: Planar compact sets with dim_H E > 4/3 have distance sets of positive Lebesgue measure. Planar only.
events.remains: Planar sets with dimension in (4/3, 2]: improved to 5/4 by Guth, Iosevich, Ou and Wang (2018 event below).
events.direction: Partial result toward the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Iosevich and Rudnev, 'Endpoint bounds for the non-isotropic Falconer distance problem associated with lattice-like sets', arXiv math/0409283, first submitted 16 September 2004 (single version). The abstract states that for lattice-based sets in dimensions four and higher the endpoint dim = d/2 is attained (distance set of positive Lebesgue measure), and that in three dimensions the argument is off by a logarithm. The result also extends to K-distance sets for smooth symmetric convex bodies with nonvanishing Gaussian curvature.
events.delivers: Positive Lebesgue measure of the distance set at exactly dim = d/2, for d >= 4, restricted to lattice-based (lattice-like) sets; d = 3 not reached (off by a logarithm). Not a statement about general sets.
events.remains: General compact sets of dimension d/2 in every dimension; d = 3 for the lattice class; and all sets of dimension above d/2 for general classes.
events.directly_checkable: The lattice-based class is explicit and can be checked from the paper's construction; not checked here.
events.direction: Restricted-class result that agrees with the conjecture (positive measure), and goes to the endpoint, but only for lattice-like sets. Not a general-set result.

events.what_happened: Konyagin and Laba, 'Separated sets and the Falconer conjecture for polygonal norms', arXiv math/0407503, first submitted 28 July 2004 (single version). For a symmetric convex polygon with 2K sides in the plane, there is a set in the unit square of Hausdorff dimension at least K/(K-1) whose distance set in that polygonal norm has Lebesgue measure zero. Analogue for non-Euclidean norms.
events.delivers: Counterexample to the Falconer-type positivity for polygonal norms (not the Euclidean norm). Dimension K/(K-1) > 1.
events.remains: Nothing about the Euclidean problem: this is a different question (a different norm), discounted for this bullet.
events.direction: Cuts against the analogous statement for polygonal norms; it is not a counterexample to the Euclidean conjecture, which is the bullet's question.
events.object: A compact planar set of Hausdorff dimension at least K/(K-1) whose distance set in the polygonal norm has measure zero; explicit construction in the abstract.

events.what_happened: Erdogan extended Wolff's planar method to higher dimensions: compact sets in R^d with dim_H E > d/2 + 1/3 (d >= 3) have distance sets of positive Lebesgue measure. Published in IMRN 2005(23), 1411-1425, per the Wikipedia citation. Not opened directly; taken from the Wikipedia table and the OpenAI manuscript's introduction (Erdogan2005, Thm 2).
events.delivers: Positive Lebesgue measure of the distance set for dim_H E > d/2 + 1/3, d >= 3 (per secondary citation).
events.remains: d/2 + 1/3 down to d/2 in every dimension, and the planar problem is treated separately.
events.direction: Partial result toward the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Du and Zhang, 'Sharp L^2 estimate of Schrodinger maximal function in higher dimensions', arXiv 1805.02775, first submitted 7 May 2018 (v3 13 Mar 2019, to appear in Annals of Math; Annals 189 (2019)). The abstract says the main theorem 'also gives improved results on the size of divergence set of Schrodinger solutions, the Falconer distance set problem and the spherical average Fourier decay rates'; it gives no numerical threshold for the Falconer problem in the abstract. The threshold d/2 + 1/4 + 1/(8d-4) for d >= 3 with a pinned conclusion is stated in later papers (Du-Ou-Ren-Zhang intro and the OpenAI manuscript's introduction).
events.revisions: v1 7 May 2018; v2 19 Jun 2018; v3 13 Mar 2019 (Annals).
events.delivers: Improvement for d >= 3 via a fractal L^2 restriction estimate. Per later papers: pinned distance sets have positive measure for dim_H E > d/2 + 1/4 + 1/(8d-4) (d >= 3). Restricted to pinned conclusion; no unpinned claim in the abstract.
events.remains: d/2 in every d >= 3; d = 2 is handled separately.

checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted for publication (v3 comment 'to appear in the Annals of Math'; published Annals 189 (2019) 837-861)

events.direction: Partial result toward the conjecture (pinned; d >= 3).

events.what_happened: Guth, Iosevich, Ou and Wang, 'On Falconer's distance set problem in the plane', arXiv 1808.09346, first submitted 28 August 2018 (single version). For compact planar E with dim_H E > 5/4 there is a point x in E such that the pinned distance set {|x - y| : y in E} has positive Lebesgue measure; this gives positive measure for the full distance set, since x is in E. Published in Inventiones Mathematicae 219 (2020) per the Wikipedia citation (journal not confirmed from the arXiv page).
events.revisions: Single version on arXiv (v1, 28 Aug 2018); journal version in Inventiones per Wikipedia citation.
events.delivers: Planar only (d = 2): compact E with dim_H E > 5/4 has a point x with positive-measure pinned distance set, hence Delta(E) has positive measure. Pinned existential statement.
events.remains: Planar sets with dimension in (1, 5/4] for general sets; d >= 3 (where the best threshold is d/2 + 1/4 - 1/(8d+4) with a pinned conclusion).

checked_by.who: Inventiones Mathematicae (journal of record, per the Wikipedia citation)
checked_by.what_they_did: Published (Inventiones 219(3) 2020 per Wikipedia); not confirmed from the arXiv page

events.doubts: Singh and Singh (arXiv 2608.28711, first submitted 28 Aug 2026, single version) state that 'the literal arbitrary-packet form of the refined-decoupling estimate printed in the Guth--Iosevich-Ou-Wang proof' is false, with a fixed-power counterexample, and offer a 'non circular repair' that they say closes exactly for alpha > 5/4. The claimed repair is unreviewed as far as I could find. The 5/4 threshold is still cited as the planar baseline by the 2026 papers below and by the OpenAI manuscript; the GIOW statement has not been withdrawn.
events.direction: Partial result toward the conjecture (planar, pinned, dimension above 5/4).

events.what_happened: Du, Iosevich, Ou, Wang and Zhang, 'An improved result for Falconer's distance set problem in even dimensions', arXiv 2006.06833, first submitted 11 June 2020 (v2 30 Mar 2021; 'to appear in Math. Ann.' per the arXiv page). The abstract states that for compact E in R^d with d >= 4 even and dim_H E > d/2 + 1/4, the distance set has positive Lebesgue measure. The OpenAI manuscript's introduction describes the same theorem as a pinned conclusion (Du-Iosevich-Ou-Wang-Zhang 2021, Thm 1.2); the two descriptions differ and I did not resolve which is right from the abstract alone.
events.delivers: Positive Lebesgue measure of the distance set for compact sets in even dimensions d >= 4 with dim_H E > d/2 + 1/4 (per the abstract). Even dimensions only.
events.remains: Odd dimensions d >= 3 (see Du-Ou-Ren-Zhang); the endpoint d/2; general d.
events.doubts: The abstract's distance-set conclusion and the OpenAI manuscript's 'pinned' description of the same theorem disagree; the full text would settle which is the statement.
events.direction: Partial result toward the conjecture (even d >= 4).

events.what_happened: Du, Guth, Ou, Wang, Wilson and Zhang proved the Falconer conjecture in dimension three when dim_H E > 9/5, with a pinned conclusion (Theorem 1.2 and Cor 1.11 as cited by the OpenAI manuscript's introduction). Dated 2021 from the citation key; the arXiv posting was not opened.
events.delivers: Dimension three only: dim_H E > 9/5 gives a pinned positive-measure conclusion, hence the distance set has positive measure (for compact E whose pinned point lies in E).
events.remains: Dimension three from 9/5 down to 3/2; dimensions d >= 4 and d = 2 treated elsewhere; the endpoint.
events.direction: Partial result toward the conjecture (d = 3).

events.what_happened: Shmerkin and Wang, 'On the distance sets spanned by sets of dimension d/2 in R^d', arXiv 2112.09044, first submitted 16 December 2021 (v3 13 Aug 2024, 'to appear in GAFA'). The abstract states they 'establish the dimension version of Falconer's distance set conjecture for sets of equal Hausdorff and packing dimension' in all ambient dimensions, covering Ahlfors-regular sets; in d = 2 or 3 they give explicit estimates for general Borel sets of dimension d/2 (for planar dimension 1, distance set dimension at least (sqrt5 - 1)/2).
events.revisions: v1 16 Dec 2021; v2 19 Jan 2022; v3 13 Aug 2024 (many corrections, referee suggestions; 'to appear in GAFA').
events.delivers: Dimension statement (dim_H Delta(E) = 1 at dim E = d/2) for sets with equal Hausdorff and packing dimension, all d. Not a Lebesgue-measure statement. Restricted to regular sets.
events.remains: Positive Lebesgue measure at dimension d/2 for general sets; the measure statement for regular sets at d/2 (the GAFA paper's dimension result does not assert measure).

checked_by.who: Geometric and Functional Analysis (journal of record)
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted for publication (v3 comment 'To appear in GAFA'; Springer DOI 10.1007/s00039-024-00696-5 listed in search results)

events.direction: Partial result toward the conjecture (dimension version at d/2 for regular sets).

events.what_happened: Bishop, Drillick and Ntalampekos, 'Falconer's (K,d) distance set conjecture can fail for strictly convex sets K in R^d', published in Rev. Mat. Iberoam. 37 (2021), no. 5, 1953-1968 (DOI 10.4171/RMI/1254), per the search summary. For any norm on R^d with countably many extreme points there is a set of Hausdorff dimension d whose distance set in that norm has zero linear measure. Analogue for non-Euclidean norms. The arXiv posting date was not established; the date recorded is the journal year.
events.delivers: Counterexample to the Falconer-type positivity for a class of non-Euclidean norms; not the Euclidean norm.
events.remains: Nothing about the Euclidean problem; discounted for this bullet as a different question (different norm).
events.direction: Cuts against the analogous statement for non-Euclidean norms; not a counterexample to the Euclidean conjecture.
events.object: A set E in R^d of Hausdorff dimension d whose distance set under a given norm (with countably many extreme points) has zero linear measure; the existence is from the paper, not checked here.

events.what_happened: Du, Ou, Ren and Zhang, 'New improvement to Falconer distance set problem in higher dimensions', arXiv 2309.04103, first submitted 8 September 2023 (v2 22 October 2024, 'slightly changed the introduction'). For compact E in R^d with d >= 3 and dim_H E > d/2 + 1/4 - 1/(8d+4), some point x in E has a pinned distance set of positive Lebesgue measure; since x is in E, the full distance set then has positive measure. Also lower bounds for pinned distance-set dimension in a range below the threshold. Preprint; journal publication status not found.
events.revisions: v1 8 Sep 2023; v2 22 Oct 2024 ('33 pages; slightly changed the introduction').
events.delivers: Positive Lebesgue measure of the pinned distance set (and hence the full distance set) for compact sets in d >= 3 with dim_H E > d/2 + 1/4 - 1/(8d+4). Restricted to d >= 3; strictly above d/2 for each d.
events.remains: The threshold d/2 itself, for each d >= 3; the planar case d = 2 (see GIOW, Liu 2026); general Borel sets if the compact reduction is not used.
events.direction: Partial result toward the conjecture (d >= 3, pinned, strict inequality above d/2).

events.what_happened: Minh-Quy Pham, 'On Falconer type functions and the distance set problem', arXiv 2510.15118, first submitted 16 October 2025 (v2 27 February 2026, described on the arXiv page as incorporating referee's comments). Results: (i) if B lies in a hyperplane and dim_H A + dim_H B > n (compact sets in R^n, n >= 2), the two-set distance set Delta(A,B) has positive Lebesgue measure, with a sharp threshold; (ii) for product sets A = A1 x A2 in R^m x R^(n-m) with A2 a Salem set and dim_H A > n/2, the distance set has positive measure; (iii) Falconer-type functions recovering a sharp result of Koh, Pham and Shen (J. Funct. Anal. 286 (2024)) for quadratic polynomials in three variables.
events.revisions: v1 16 Oct 2025; v2 27 Feb 2026 (referee's comments incorporated, per arXiv page).
events.delivers: Positive measure for restricted classes only: two-set distance sets with one set in a hyperplane (sharp threshold); product sets with a Salem factor; a class of smooth Falconer-type functions. Not general sets.
events.remains: The Falconer conjecture for general compact sets in R^d for every d >= 2 (not addressed by the abstract). The product-set and hyperplane classes are the restriction.

checked_by.who: Unnamed referee (per the arXiv v2 comment 'incorporating referee's comments')
checked_by.qualification: Not named on the arXiv page
checked_by.what_they_did: Comments incorporated into v2 (27 Feb 2026); the journal and referee are not identified

events.direction: Partial result toward the conjecture, in restricted classes; cuts toward positive measure.

events.what_happened: Bochen Liu, 'Lebesgue measure of distance sets with regular pins and multi-scale Mizohata-Takeuchi-type estimates', arXiv 2603.15328 (sole author; v1 16 Mar 2026, v2 25 Apr 2026, v3 16 Jul 2026). For Borel planar sets E and F with dim_H E > 1, dim_H E + dim_H F > 2 and F with equal Hausdorff and packing dimension, there is y in F whose pinned distance set has positive Lebesgue measure. The arXiv abstract says this 'settles the regular case of the distance set problem in the plane'. A talk listing (City University of Hong Kong, scheduled 16 June 2026) gives the same claim. The OpenAI manuscript's introduction reads Liu's theorem as yielding the planar conclusion when F = E for sets with equal Hausdorff and packing dimension above one.
events.revisions: v1 16 Mar 2026; v2 25 Apr 2026 (a Proposition relabelled, per arXiv comments); v3 16 Jul 2026 (a typo in a statement involving omega_Q(T) corrected, per arXiv comments).
events.delivers: Planar only (d = 2). Pinned conclusion at some y in F. With F = E this gives positive measure of the full distance set for planar sets with equal Hausdorff and packing dimension above 1 (the regular case). Restricted to regular sets.
events.remains: Planar general (non-regular) Borel sets above the threshold; the full planar conjecture at dimension 1; all d >= 3. The general planar threshold remains 5/4 (GIOW).
events.doubts: Revised twice (v2 relabelled a Proposition; v3 corrected a typo in a statement, per arXiv comments). I read only the abstract page, so I could not confirm that the v1 and v3 hypotheses are identical. The talk abstracts say 'settles the regular case'; the arXiv abstract states the pinned conclusion. The OpenAI manuscript cites this paper as a method precedent and reads its theorem as above.
events.direction: Partial result toward the conjecture (planar, regular sets, pinned conclusion, which yields the unpinned conclusion when F = E).

events.what_happened: Jonathan M. Fraser and Thang Pham, 'On Fourier decay and the distance set problem', arXiv 2604.19486, first submitted 21 April 2026 (single version, 29 pages). The abstract states: a Borel set with Fourier dimension at least 2 has a distance set of full Hausdorff dimension; a Borel set with Fourier spectrum at least d/4 + 1 at theta = 1/2 has a distance set of full Hausdorff dimension (this can hold with Fourier dimension zero when d >= 4); under mild assumptions the authors 'beat the d/2 dimension threshold in dimensions d >= 5'.
events.delivers: Dimension statements (full Hausdorff dimension of the distance set) for Fourier-analytic classes (Fourier dimension at least 2, or the Fourier spectrum condition), in dimensions d >= 5 beyond d/2. Not a Lebesgue-measure statement as the abstract is written. Restricted classes.
events.remains: General Borel sets above d/2 with no Fourier hypothesis; the Lebesgue-measure conclusion for the stated classes (the abstract states dimension, not measure).
events.direction: Partial result toward the conjecture (dimension, restricted classes); cuts in the conjectured direction.

events.what_happened: Thang Pham, Chun-Yen Shen and Boqing Xue, 'On Erdos-Falconer distance problem in even dimensions', arXiv 2607.17324, first submitted 19 July 2026 (single version). Works over finite fields F_q (odd q), not the Euclidean setting: an extraction theorem reducing the even-dimensional finite-field Erdos-Falconer conjecture to the planar case, with pinned thresholds d/2 + 1/4 over prime fields and (d+1)/2 + 1/10 over arbitrary finite fields. Listed under math.NT with math.CA and math.CO cross-lists.
events.delivers: Results for finite fields only. Says nothing about the Euclidean conjecture as stated on the arXiv page.
events.remains: The Euclidean conjecture is untouched by this paper. Discounted as a different question (finite field analogue).
events.direction: Not about the Euclidean problem; analogue only.

events.what_happened: Shalender Singh and Vishnu Priya Singh, 'Repairing the refined-decoupling proof of the 5/4 planar pinned Falconer theorem', arXiv 2608.28711, first submitted 28 August 2026 (single version, 25 pages, math.CA). The abstract says the literal arbitrary-packet form of the refined-decoupling estimate printed in the Guth-Iosevich-Ou-Wang proof is false (with a fixed-power counterexample), and gives a 'non circular repair of the original proof route' whose analytic input is an arbitrary-packet theorem proved from weighted l^2 decoupling; the energy argument is said to close exactly for alpha > 5/4. The authors note that the pinned theorem itself is not contradicted and is known through later microlocal methods.
events.delivers: Claims a repaired proof of the planar pinned 5/4 statement (the same statement as GIOW). Adds no new threshold; concerns the existing planar baseline.
events.remains: Nothing new for the conjecture: the planar threshold remains 5/4 in the claimed repair; general planar sets at 1 remain open.
events.doubts: The authors' own claim is that a printed estimate in the GIOW proof is false; the repair is the authors' and I found no public check of it. Authors' qualifications are not stated in the sources I read.
events.direction: Concerns the planar baseline; supports the 5/4 threshold by repair rather than moving it.

events.what_happened: Alex Iosevich and Alexia Yavicoli, 'Improved dimension bounds for Falconer's distance problem in the plane', arXiv 2610.05500, submitted 4 October 2026 (single version, 133 pages, math.CA). For compact analytic planar E with t = dim_H E > 1: dim_H Delta E >= 4/5 + eta_0 for an absolute, non-explicit eta_0 > 0; an explicit bound (t^2 - 2t + 5)/(2t^2 - 7t + 10) for 1 < t <= (11 - sqrt 41)/4, reaching 7/8 at the right endpoint; and for pinned distance sets, dim_H Delta_x E >= 0.7813... for x outside an exceptional set of dimension at most one.
events.delivers: Lower bounds on the Hausdorff dimension of the distance set for analytic planar sets (dimension quantity, not Lebesgue measure); pinned dimension bounds for almost every base point. Restricted to analytic planar sets.
events.remains: Positive Lebesgue measure of Delta E for planar sets above 5/4 and in general; the dimension bounds do not give measure; all d >= 3.
events.direction: Partial dimension bound toward the conjecture; does not address the measure question in the bullet.

events.what_happened: OpenAI released, in the public openai/math GitHub repository (family 073 'The Falconer distance conjecture', pinned commit adc7f12), a manuscript titled 'The Falconer distance conjecture in all dimensions' with author line 'OpenAI'. The paper's abstract reads 'We resolve the Falconer distance conjecture in every dimension.' The main statement, as the Lean formalisation and the paper's introduction state it, is: for every integer d >= 2 and compact E in R^d with dim_H E > d/2, the distance set has positive Lebesgue measure (the paper's Theorem 1.1, unpinned, with no endpoint assertion at d/2). The planar case is included as d = 2. The manuscript is dated 23 September 2026 (on the paper, in the file path, and in the BibTeX entry), but it became public in the 6 October 2026 release of 722 manuscripts (719 after three later withdrawals) that OpenAI said were generated by an internal model. Lean: a Comparator challenge file ComparatorChallenges/FalconerAllDimensions.lean states theorem falconer_distance_conjecture with a 'sorry' by design; the solution is OAI.Falconer.falconer_distance_conjecture in OAI/MeasureTheory/Falconer/Campaign123PlanarFurstenbergProof.lean. A third-party repository (CoolRmal/falconer-all-dimensions) isolates the same formalisation and reports a Comparator pass on 6 October 2026 (run 37545204340); its log ends 'Lean default kernel accepts the solution', 'Your solution is okay!', 'Finished with result: success'. The README lists the permitted axioms as propext, Quot.sound and Classical.choice.
events.revisions: Paper date 23 Sep 2026 (paper, file path, BibTeX). Public release 6 Oct 2026 (repo). Main-branch history.md 'October 7, 2026' entry: three manuscripts withdrawn (Algebraicity of Weil classes on split abelian eightfolds; Kuga-Satake correspondences for K3 surfaces; rational Hodge conjecture for products of K3 surfaces) and 14 others revised; none of the withdrawn or revised manuscripts named in that entry is the Falconer manuscript. Revision status of the Falconer manuscript after 7 Oct 2026 was not established.
events.delivers: Claims the full conjecture: for every integer d >= 2 and compact E in R^d with dim_H E > d/2 (strict), Delta(E) = {|x - y| : x, y in E} has positive Lebesgue measure. Covers d = 2 and every d >= 3. Restricted to compact E in the paper and formal statement. The paper cites as inputs: Orponen-Shmerkin 2023 multiscale incidence theorem (retained input, Thm 1.3); Orponen-Shmerkin-Wang tube formulation; Ren 2023 radial and plate-concentration methods; Orponen 2019 finite-energy method (adapted); Mattila 1995 Plancherel (eq. 12.4); and background results Falconer 1985, Mattila 1987, Bourgain 1994, Wolff 1999, Erdogan 2005, Du-Zhang 2019, Du-Guth-Ou-Wang-Wilson-Zhang 2021, Guth-Iosevich-Ou-Wang 2020, Du-Iosevich-Ou-Wang-Zhang 2021, Du-Ou-Ren-Zhang 2024, Shmerkin-Wang 2025, Liu 2026, Borges-Ou-Pasquariello 2026, Keleti-Shmerkin 2019, and an OpenAI distinct-distances theorem (OpenAIDistinctDistances2026) cited as a parallel result. The introduction says the proof 'does not invoke a decoupling theorem or any earlier distance theorem at an improved threshold'. The formal statement of the Lean target is the paper's stated theorem. The Lean proof's planar input is a PublishedPlanarFurstenberg specialisation; the file says it is proved in Lean (publishedPlanarFurstenberg_proved), and the file's comment describes it as 'the precise planar Furstenberg specialization used by the all-dimensional Falconer proof', 'by the finite multiscale incidence argument'. I did not read the definition of PublishedPlanarFurstenberg or the three imported modules.
events.remains: On the manuscript's own claim, nothing that problem_asks lists is left open. Items not established from the sources I read: whether the Lean input PublishedPlanarFurstenberg is exactly the published Orponen-Shmerkin theorem (proved in Lean) or a restated hypothesis; whether the three imported Lean modules are sorry-free and axiom-clean; whether the paper's argument is correct; whether the statement was intended as a compact-set or general-set claim.

checked_by.qualification: Not stated in the sources read; the work is a Lean and Erdos-similarity project, not a harmonic-analysis paper
checked_by.what_they_did: Re-checked OpenAI's Lean proof of the Falconer statement in a verify/ directory and uses FalconerStatement as an explicit hypothesis (Theorem A, Lemma 3.3, Proposition 3.2, Proposition C(iii)) in a separate 2026 paper; the README says the work was 'prepared with substantial assistance from Claude (Anthropic)'. This is a check of the formal proof only, not a reading of the mathematics.

events.time_since_posted: 5 days at the time of research (6 to 11 Oct 2026)

machine_checked.system: Lean 4 (4.34.1 per the CoolRmal README) with Mathlib pinned; Comparator challenge harness
machine_checked.note: Log reports 'Lean default kernel accepts the solution' and 'Your solution is okay!' with exported declarations including OAI.Falconer.falconer_distance_conjecture. The only 'declaration uses sorry' warning in the log I could read is at ComparatorChallenges/FalconerAllDimensions.lean:11:8, which is the challenge statement and is sorry by design. sorry_free is null because the three imported modules and PublishedPlanarFurstenberg were not read. The Comparator date (6 Oct 2026) comes from the README; the log had no timestamp I could read. The log was read through a summarising fetch tool, not as raw text.

events.directly_checkable: The formal statement is a single short declaration: for every natural d with 2 <= d, every compact E in EuclideanSpace R (Fin d), if (d:ENNReal)/2 < dimH E then 0 < volume {r : R | exists x in E, exists y in E, dist x y = r}. Whether this matches the bullet can be checked by reading that line. The argument itself is in the paper's sections 00 to 10 (LaTeX source); sections 01 to 08 were not read.
events.doubts: (1) Not peer reviewed and not posted to arXiv; no journal or referee. (2) Released in bulk: OpenAI's spokesperson said roughly half the results were released before formal confirmation (Retraction Watch, 8 Oct 2026). The same release contained a sign error that invalidated one manuscript and two dependent papers, found by an internal audit the day after release (Retraction Watch; history.md). That error is not reported to involve the Falconer manuscript, but it shows the batch was not vetted before release. (3) The paper's own key steps are parameter-dependent: 'sufficiently small in terms of d, chi, beta', 'for all sufficiently large N', 'the o(1) term may depend on B and the Q_j', 'a dimensional constant must be large enough for the branch bound' (section 09/10 excerpts). Checking those is nontrivial and I found no public check of them. (4) The planar input is a 'PublishedPlanarFurstenberg' specialisation; if it is a stronger hypothesis than the published statement, the Lean certificate would not transfer to the published result. Not established either way. (5) The result would close a problem that the specialist literature treated as open with a large jump: the best general planar result is 5/4 (pinned), and the best general d >= 3 result is d/2 + 1/4 - 1/(8d+4) (pinned). The paper says it does not use decoupling; prior improvements used decoupling and Fourier restriction. (6) No specialist has publicly engaged with the argument as of 11 Oct 2026. Iosevich and Yavicoli's preprint (4 Oct 2026) predates the release and does not respond to it. I found no comment from Iosevich, Shmerkin, Orponen, Wang, Liu, Ren or Tao on the Falconer manuscript. Terence Tao's blog hosts a guest post by the Association for Human Mathematics on the 6 October release that does not name the Falconer result, and Tao's own 9 October post is about Lean reliability and does not name it. (7) One public blog reaction calls the Falconer manuscript 'the solution to the Falconer distance problem' with no check (Hyunwoo Kwon, undated, written after 6 Oct); this is an endorsement of the announcement, not a verification. (8) One aggregator (Wikipedia, edited 7 Oct 2026) reports it as 'a preprint claiming to prove the conjecture', which is the cautious description.
events.direction: Claims the full conjecture: the distance set has positive measure for every compact set with dim_H E > d/2 in every d >= 2. This is the direction the conjecture asserts (positive measure), not a counterexample; the endpoint d/2 is not claimed.

systems.name: an internal OpenAI model
systems.what_it_did: The repository's README says it 'contains mathematical manuscripts and supporting proof artifacts produced by an internal OpenAI model', and that 'the vast majority of results were obtained with the same procedure using an unreleased internal OpenAI model'. The Falconer family (073) is not among the exceptions the README lists (a zero-free region for the Riemann zeta function; proof of the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties) and is not among the ten families with released reasoning summaries (007, 017, 087, 102, 159, 197, 221, 271, 287, 362), but the README does not name family 073 as produced by that procedure. The Falconer paper's author line is 'OpenAI' and the paper names no model; the paper's abstract and introduction name no model and say nothing about how the argument was produced. Whether the model produced the Lean formalisation of this family is not stated. The model is described as internal and unreleased; the name is not given beyond 'an internal OpenAI model'.
systems.basis_quote: This repository contains mathematical manuscripts and supporting proof artifacts produced by an internal OpenAI model.

events.what_happened: Eyvindur Ari Palsson and Jian-An Wang, 'The Erdos-Falconer distance problem in the integer lattice', arXiv 2610.10665, submitted 7 October 2026 (single version, math.MG). A discrete problem on Z^d motivated by Magyar's discrete analogue of the Furstenberg-Katznelson-Weiss result and by the Falconer problem. Uses l^p-improving inequalities for discrete spherical averages. States that neither the Erdos nor the Falconer results appear to imply anything for their pinned variant.

disputes.summary: Status conflict rather than a priority dispute. Wikipedia (edited 7 Oct 2026) reports the OpenAI preprint as 'claiming to prove the conjecture'. ProofAtlas (status checked 7 Aug 2026, before the release) says the full conjecture 'remains open' and cites Liu 2026 as a 2026 seminar result. Iosevich and Yavicoli (submitted 4 Oct 2026, two days before the release) give dimension bounds and do not treat the full conjecture as settled. No author or expert has publicly disputed the OpenAI claim in print as of 11 Oct 2026, and no priority claim competes with it.

summary: The Wikipedia article (edited 7 October 2026) reports that OpenAI published a preprint claiming to prove the conjecture. The primary source is the openai/math repository: family 073 (lean/docs/073.md) and a manuscript 'The Falconer distance conjecture in all dimensions' (LaTeX author line 'OpenAI'; dated 23 September 2026; public in the 6 October 2026 release of 722 manuscripts, now 719 after three withdrawals). Its abstract is one sentence, 'We resolve the Falconer distance conjecture in every dimension', and the introduction states the theorem for compact E with dim_H E > d/2 and no endpoint claim. I read the LaTeX source's introduction (00), ledger (09) and assembly (10) sections through a fetch tool, which summarises rather than quoting verbatim; the PDF returned binary and I did not read it as text. The introduction names its inputs: the Orponen-Shmerkin 2023 multiscale incidence theorem (retained input), the Orponen-Shmerkin-Wang tube formulation, Ren 2023, Orponen 2019 (adapted), and, in the assembly section, Mattila 1995 Plancherel as the only external citation there; it says the proof does not invoke decoupling or any earlier distance theorem at an improved threshold. The Lean target file ComparatorChallenges/FalconerAllDimensions.lean states the bullet's claim (compact E in EuclideanSpace R (Fin d), d >= 2, dimH E > d/2, volume of the distance set > 0) with 'sorry' by design. The solution OAI.Falconer.falconer_distance_conjecture lives in OAI/MeasureTheory/Falconer/Campaign123PlanarFurstenbergProof.lean, which imports three further modules and uses a PublishedPlanarFurstenberg specialisation; I did not read those. A third-party repository (CoolRmal/falconer-all-dimensions) reports a Comparator run on 6 October 2026 whose log ends 'Lean default kernel accepts the solution' and 'Your solution is okay!', with axioms restricted to propext, Quot.sound and Classical.choice; the log's only sorry warning that I read is at the challenge statement line. The log was read through a summarising tool and its timestamp was not visible, so the 6 October date is the README's. Human engagement: Harald Schilly re-checked the Lean proof and builds on it as a hypothesis, which is a check of the formal proof and not of the mathematics; no specialist in geometric measure theory has publicly commented on the argument (searches to 11 October 2026 found Iosevich, Shmerkin, Orponen, Wang, Liu, Ren and Tao silent on it). The only public endorsement I found is an undated blog reaction calling it 'the solution to the Falconer distance problem' with no check. Batch context: OpenAI said roughly half the results were released before formal confirmation; three sibling manuscripts (Hodge-related) were withdrawn for a sign error found by an internal audit, and 14 others were revised. The main-branch history entry for 7 October lists those withdrawals and revisions and does not include the Falconer manuscript; news reports do not either, so its status after 7 October is not established. Partial results in the record: planar pinned 5/4 (GIOW, 2018), whose refined-decoupling proof a 28 August 2026 preprint says contains a false printed estimate with a claimed repair; Liu (16 March 2026) planar regular-case, pinned, which gives the unpinned planar statement when F = E; Du-Ou-Ren-Zhang (2023) d >= 3 pinned threshold d/2 + 1/4 - 1/(8d+4); Du-Iosevich-Ou-Wang-Zhang (2020) even d >= 4 threshold d/2 + 1/4, where the abstract states the distance-set conclusion but the OpenAI introduction calls it pinned (I did not resolve which); Shmerkin-Wang (2021) dimension version at d/2 for regular sets; Iosevich-Rudnev (2004) endpoint for lattice-like sets; Pham (2025), and Fraser-Pham (2026) for restricted classes; Iosevich-Yavicoli (4 October 2026) planar dimension bounds, not measure. Discounted as different questions: Konyagin-Laba (2004) and Bishop-Drillick-Ntalampekos (2021) for non-Euclidean norms; Pham-Shen-Xue (2026) for finite fields; Palsson-Wang (2026) for the integer lattice. Close calls: (1) Lean-accepted versus human-verified. The record keeps these separate; a judging pass may read the Lean certificate as a resolution or as a claim pending human check, and the sources do not settle which. (2) Whether PublishedPlanarFurstenberg is the published theorem proved in Lean or a stronger input: unresolved here. (3) Compact versus general sets: the bullet does not say compact, the paper and Lean statement do, and the conjecture is usually stated for compact or Borel sets. (4) The 5/4 baseline: whether the Singh-Singh repair holds is unreviewed. AI involvement: the only system named is 'an internal OpenAI model' (no version or name given). The README's sentence that the repository's manuscripts were 'produced by an internal OpenAI model' is OpenAI's own account; the Falconer family is not among the listed exceptions, but the README does not name it individually, and the paper names only 'OpenAI'. Other AI-related items found and not counted here: OpenAI's May 2026 unit distance disproof (a different problem), OpenAI's August 2026 ten-results announcement (Falconer not among them), and Schilly's 2026 paper, which credits 'substantial assistance from Claude (Anthropic)' in preparing a different paper.
competing_reading: A Lean kernel accepting the exact statement, with a restricted axiom list and a statement readable in one line, is a stronger machine guarantee than most human-written resolutions carry. On that reading the bullet was settled on 6 October 2026, and the open items (the PublishedPlanarFurstenberg definition, the imported modules, the compact-set restriction) are verification details rather than doubts. The opposite reading: a Lean certificate verifies only the formal statement relative to its inputs, and the planar Furstenberg input carries most of the difficulty; the manuscript is unrefereed; a batch that shipped a sign error in three sibling manuscripts within a day was not vetted; and no specialist has engaged. On that reading the honest status is 'claimed, Lean-accepted, not accepted by the field', and the planar 5/4 literature would also be affected by the Singh-Singh claim.
what_would_settle_it: (1) A geometric measure theorist reading the manuscript's sections 01 to 10, especially the two-depth potential, the oscillatory graph reductions and the angular bound, and reporting whether each step holds; the Orponen and Shmerkin authors would be the natural readers. (2) For the Lean side: the three imported modules (Incidence/OriginalBlockIncidence, Estimates/OriginalWeakCosts, Estimates/OneInputMain) and PublishedPlanarFurstenberg read in full, showing them sorry-free with the transitive axioms, and a comparison of PublishedPlanarFurstenberg with the published Orponen-Shmerkin 2023 statement. (3) The openai/math history and CONTENTS entries for family 073 after 7 October 2026: any withdrawal, revision or erratum. (4) A referee or journal decision, or a public verification by a named expert. (5) A check of the Singh-Singh repair of the GIOW refined-decoupling estimate, since the planar 5/4 literature is a baseline for the claim.
